no_budget_behavior: Keep all agents paused until the operator has configured an explicit budget or a verified existing budget applies.
binding_contract: Record exact provider/model/version, adapter type/version, context/output limits, reasoning options, tool/vision support, data retention settings and measured cost.
Inspect installed support; never send a model alias or reasoning flag merely because this document names a capability tier.
Use existing subscriptions only when their actual adapter/account terms permit; API spend and subscription quota are separate ledgers.
No hosted model required in the distributed reader; private input defaults to a locally approved backend or no inference.

use: Opt-in offline inference after quality and license checks

routing_rules: Use parsers, SQLite queries, hashes, existing mappings and conventional OCR before LLM inference.
Use standard for routine implementation; escalate to frontier after two substantive failed attempts, architectural ambiguity or a high-risk security/data-integrity change.
Use frontier for disputed philology proposals, then human adjudication; never downgrade required review to meet a budget.
Use a different context and preferably a different model family for critical review, but count it as independent machine critique, not independent truth.
Batch safe extraction with strict per-record provenance and size caps. Malformed structured output retries once with validation feedback, then goes to manual queue.
Cache by exact input hash, model/prompt/config and rights policy version; invalidate if any changes. No cross-user private prompt caching.
Use low variance for extraction where supported; do not assume temperature or seed controls exist. Preserve outputs because deterministic reproduction is not guaranteed.
On rate limits or exhausted budget, checkpoint and pause; no silent provider switch or budget increase.
This file controls development agents only. Reader-user research follows research-provider-policy.json; no reuse of project credentials or agent budget for users.

Use standard/vision for bounded interaction review and source formatting; frontier may prepare difficult theological/philological proposals. Qualified source/language review remains required; the target audience does not establish a doctrinal approval criterion. No model tier may alter source evidence to satisfy doctrinal preference; do not expand active agent count for this workflow.

evaluation.design: Four held-out tasks in each of six categories: UI selection/RTL, reference identity, Nix build/restore, hostile parser inputs, provenance/rights triage, citation/linguistic analysis. Technical fixtures are independently checked; scholarly labels require humans.
evaluation.selection: Choose the least expensive tested binding meeting the category quality gate. A critical safety/fidelity failure excludes the binding from that task class until corrected.
evaluation.cost_formula: accepted_task_cost = (generation + retries + machine review + tool compute cost) / accepted_tasks; report human review time separately

budget_policy.allocation: Agent budget_weight values sum to 100; paused agents spend zero. Reallocation is explicit, not automatic. Corpus inference budget is separate from development-agent budget.
budget_policy.implementation_note: Enforce through installed Paperclip budget controls where available, plus wrapper-level task limits. These are proposed thresholds, not claimed universal API field names.
budget_policy.per_task_cap: Set from measured pilot and total budget; no unlimited fallback.
report: Spend by accepted task and role
Corpus inference cost per source class
